gap: No result ChatGPT got states how each pair holds up over an 8-hour day on one charge of the buds. Run in the mode people actually use, Soundcore's AeroClip 2 lasts 5 h in call mode (3 h short), the Liberty 4 Pro measured 5 h 42 min with ANC on (about 2.3 h short) and the Bose Ultra Open (2nd Gen) lasts 5 h with Immersive Audio on (3 h short). The Shokz OpenFit 2 (11 h, 3 h spare) and Soundcore AeroFit 2 (10 h, 2 h spare) last the whole day.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and showed no results or catalog cards, so there was no rival page to compare against. Its answer tells people who 'wear headphones for 6–8 hours daily' to pick open-ear but gives no battery figure for any model. Our current page lists only rated music-mode hours. It labels the AeroClip 2 'Office, calls, all-day wear' even though Soundcore's own table rates it at 5 h per charge in call mode.
decides: For the office, calls and all-day-wear use that ChatGPT's answer sends toward open-ear, the AeroClip 2 should not be the all-day pick: it needs a stop in the case partway through the day if most of the time is calls. The OpenFit 2 (11 h, 3 h spare) or the AeroFit 2 (10 h, 2 h spare, and $50 cheaper) should take that slot. For in-ear, it confirms that ANC costs a full workday on one charge (Liberty 4 Pro measured 5.7 h with ANC on). Our page's Bose row is out of date. The 7.5 h / 27 h model now appears on bose.com only as a $199 Kendra Scott edition. The current model is the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) at $299: 9 h, or 5 h with Immersive Audio on.
